deep.reconstruction:
The sheet mixes unrelated jottings. The main item is a heuristic about the Euler product of a quadratic L-series at s = 1, in the upright left and centre columns.

(A) Euler product for a quadratic L-series at s = 1 (left and centre, upright ink).
- Riemann starts from prod 1/(1-1/p).
- He splits the odd primes not dividing D into two classes: p with (D/p) = +1 and q with (D/q) = -1.
- The Euler product of L(1, chi_D) = sum (D/n)/n is then prod_p 1/(1-1/p) * prod_q 1/(1+1/q).
- The written line is prod_{p<K^m} 1/(1-1/p) * prod_{q<K} 1/(1+1/q) = m^{1/2} sum (D/n) 1/n. There is a crossed-out bound 'q<K^m' on the first factor, and the line prod_{p<K^m} 1/(1-1/p) appears below. So the p-product runs to K^m and the q-product only to K.
- Taking logarithms gives -log(1-1/p) - log(1+1/q), approximately +1/p - 1/q.
- He then replaces each prime sum by an integral. He assumes the primes have density 1/log x and that each class takes half of them, so sum 1/p over a range is about (1/2) int dx/(x log x).
- With the different cutoffs, the excess of the p-sum over the range K < p < K' = K^m is (1/2) int_K^{K'} dx/(x log x) = (1/2)(log log K' - log log K) = log (log K'/log K)^{1/2} = log m^{1/2}.
- Hence, as K -> infinity, the unequally truncated product tends to m^{1/2} L(1, chi_D), not to L(1, chi_D).
- The centre line prod_{q<K} 1/(1-1/q) = m^{1/2} records the same fact for one half-density class over [K, K^m]. My reading: the range is implicit. Over all primes in that range the product would tend to m (Mertens-type ratio); over a half-density class it tends to m^{1/2}.
- Sigma log(1-1/p) and int dx/log x (the logarithmic integral) are noted nearby.
- In substance this is the multiplicative analogue of the rearrangement of a conditionally convergent series. Compare the alternating harmonic series: taking more positive than negative terms shifts the sum by (1/2) log of the ratio. Here the conditionally convergent Euler product at s = 1 is multiplied by m^{1/2} when the two classes of primes are truncated at K^m and K.

(B) Upright, top left: tg x = b x^3/(x^4 + a^4).
- This is a transcendental equation tan x = rational function. The notes n pi and (n + 1/2) pi indicate the location of its roots.
- The right side tends to 0 as x -> infinity, so the large roots approach n pi.
- 'log K = infinity' is a stray note.

(C) Centre: (x1 y2 - x2 y1)/(y2 - y1) = (x1 y2 - x2 y1)/(y2 - y1).
- This continues the previous page: the x-intercept of the line through (x1, y1) and (x2, y2).
- x = x1 - y1 (x2 - x1)/(y2 - y1) = (x1 y2 - x2 y1)/(y2 - y1).

(D) Upside-down ink: int dx/sqrt(1 - x^4).
- The factorisation 1 - x^4 = (1 - x^2)(1 + x^2) is noted. This is the lemniscatic integral; 'k =' is the modulus to be determined.
- Periods are written as n + m omega, corrected to (n + m i) omega. This is the square period lattice of the lemniscatic function, which has complex multiplication by i.

(E) Upside-down pencil: pv = const, so log p + log v = log c, so dp/p + dv/v = 0.
- This is Boyle-Mariotte; dp/dv and d rho/dt also appear.
- It is probably connected with gas dynamics (cf. his 1859 paper on finite-amplitude waves).

(F) Sketches: a square with an inscribed circle, a curvilinear triangle, and a polygonal pencil figure.

(G) Rotated Kurrent text: a draft (letter or apology) addressed to the Academy.
- It mentions 'seit dem Sommer 1859' and 'in meiner Arbeit'.
- This suggests a date around 1859-60, consistent with Riemann's election to the Berlin Academy and his prime-number paper. The text is only partly legible.
errors: Line '1/2 log log K' - log K' as transcribed is inconsistent. From the integral it should read 1/2 log log K' - 1/2 log log K, as the next line log(log K'/log K)^{1/2} confirms.
The equality prod_{p<K^m} prod_{q<K} = m^{1/2} sum (D/n)/n is only an asymptotic statement as K -> infinity.

It rests on the unproved, at the time, assumption that primes split with relative density 1/2 between (D/p) = +1 and -1 in the strong sense that sum over primes of (D/p)/p converges. That follows from PNT in progressions (Mertens 1874/1895 and later).
Replacing -log(1-1/p) by 1/p is fine; the error terms converge absolutely.
'prod_{q<K} 1/(1-1/q) = m^{1/2}' is literally false as written. It must mean the product over q in (K, K^m], asymptotically.
The tan-equation note gives no derivation, so there is nothing to check beyond root locations near n pi.

results.what: Euler product of L(1,chi_D) split into primes with (D/p) = +/-1; truncating the two classes at K^m and K multiplies the limit by m^{1/2}, derived via sum 1/p ~ 1/2 int dx/(x log x)
results.modern_name: Conditional convergence / rearrangement of the Euler product at s=1; Mertens-type estimate sum_{p<=x, chi(p)=1} 1/p = (1/2) log log x + C
results.usually_credited_to: Mertens (1874, 1895) for rigorous Mertens theorems and convergence of the Euler product of L(1,chi); heuristic density arguments go back to Gauss, Legendre, Dirichlet and Chebyshev; rearrangement phenomenon for series to Riemann (1854) and Dirichlet

deep.surprise_reason: Riemann treats the Euler product of a quadratic Dirichlet L-series at s = 1 as conditionally convergent. He shows, heuristically, that unequal truncation of the split and inert prime classes multiplies the value by m^{1/2}, using Mertens-type half-density estimates. This is a nice unpublished multiplicative analogue of his rearrangement theorem and anticipates Mertens' estimates (1874/1895). However, it is heuristic, the density assumptions were folklore (Dirichlet, Chebyshev), and Riemann's 1859 prime work makes such interests expected.

transcription_corrections: First product line: subscripts are p (with a crossed-out bound 'q<K^m'), i.e. prod_p 1/(1-1/p) * prod_{q<K} 1/(1+1/q) = m^{1/2} sum (D/n) 1/n; the p-product appears to run to K^m (cf. the later line prod_{p<K^m}).
'1/2 log log K' - log K' should be read as 1/2 log log K' - (1/2) log log K; the second term is partly overwritten.
'log k = infinity' at top left is more likely 'log K = infinity', i.e. K -> infinity.
Centre line 'prod_{q<K} 1/(1-1/q) = m^{1/2}' is a statement about the q-class over the range K..K^m.
Lower right: 'n + m omega' is corrected by Riemann to '(n+mi) omega' (lemniscatic lattice); 'pi = pi [?]' is doubtful and may be a period symbol.
Kurrent block: begins with a heading like 'Entschuldigung' and contains 'seit dem Sommer 1859' and 'in meiner Arbeit'; addressed to the Akademie; largely illegible in the machine transcription.
